hero.title: Astro reaches for the stars. Mica keeps your content down to earth.

preview.title: Click the page. Edit the field.
preview.lead: The editor shows your real Astro page beside the form, with the drafts in it. A second after you stop typing, the page shows the change. Click a heading, a paragraph, an image or a date on the page, and the cursor goes to its field.

image.alt: The Mica editor with the form of the Services page on the left and the live preview of the page on the right. The page heading has an outline and the label Title, and the changed introduction has a dashed outline.

points.text: Your templates stay as they are: one line in astro.config
Changes that are not published yet have an outline of their own
Menus and settings open in a form over the page's form
In the local editor and in the self-hosted editor

how.title: One model. Forms for editors. Files for your build.
how.lead: The content model connects the editor and the website. Git connects everything else.

steps.title: Describe your content
steps.text: Write the content model in TypeScript, next to your pages. Fields, labels, help texts and rules live in one file.

steps.title: Editors fill in forms
steps.text: Mica turns the model into forms. The form saves by itself, and the page beside it shows each change. Nothing goes on the website until someone publishes.

steps.title: Publish makes one commit
steps.text: Publish commits the saved JSON, Markdoc and images to your repository, as one commit. Your build reads the files. The website never calls Mica.

capabilities.title: Real websites have photos, places and long lists.
capabilities.lead: A site with thousands of photos, a map and a list of peaks works with Mica. The content stays plain files in Git.

items.title: Photos by the thousand
items.text: Keep media in Git LFS, out of your normal history. Editors drop a whole set of photos on a field, and Mica goes on when one upload fails.

items.title: Places on a map
items.text: Editors select a place on a map, and Mica saves the zoom with it. Your pages draw the same view with MapLibre and OpenFreeMap, or a style of your own.

items.title: Files, not only images
items.text: Accept GPX, KML, GeoJSON, ZIP and CSV next to images and PDF. Mica checks each file by its bytes, and your build reads them.

items.title: Reference data
items.text: Link an entry to one of thousands of items from a JSON or CSV file that Mica never edits: peaks, regions, product codes.

items.title: Live preview and links
items.text: The editor shows the real page beside the form, with the drafts in it, in the local and in the self-hosted editor. A click on the page opens its field. Each entry can also link to its published page.

items.title: Content in its own repository
items.text: Mount the content as a Git submodule. Mica works in that repository and never commits in the website repository.

audiences.title: Calm for editors. Plain for developers.

groups.title: For editors
groups.text: Clear forms with the labels and help that your developer wrote. Rich text, photo sets, files, places on a map, and lists that you can reorder. No Git words, no YAML.

points.text: See each change on the real page before you publish
Click a text on the page to edit its field
Choose what goes on the website
Keep mine or use theirs when two people edit

groups.title: For developers
groups.text: The model is TypeScript. The content is JSON, Markdoc and media in your repository, in Git LFS if you like. Astro reads it at build time, with types.

points.text: No database, no content API, no webhook
A live preview with no change to your templates
mica check and a model check in your CI
One reviewable commit for each publish

agents.title: Your agent edits too. It saves drafts, like everybody else.
agents.lead: Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code or any other MCP client can read your content model and change your content. It follows the rules of the editor. A person publishes the drafts.

points.text: Reads the content model, and Mica checks every value
Saves drafts. Publishing by an agent is off, unless you turn it on
Sends the revision it read, so it never overwrites a newer save
Finds items of reference data, and uploads photos and files
Local: npx mica start serves the tools. Self-hosted: you opt in, and each person allows each agent

scale.title: A small team, with real numbers.
scale.lead: Tests check these numbers. Above them, Mica can work, but nobody measured it yet.

link.label: Read the scope and the limits

run.title: On your laptop, or on your server.
run.lead: Both edit the same files in the same repository. Start with one, and add the other when you need it.

options.title: Local editor
options.text: Runs on your machine, next to astro dev, with the live preview of your drafts. Publish commits and pushes with your own Git credentials.

needs.text: A Git repository, and Git LFS if you use it
No sign-in, no account, no database

options.title: Self-hosted editor
options.text: One container on your server, and a second one for the live preview. Editors sign in through your identity provider, for example Google. Mica keeps its own Git clone, with Git LFS built in.

needs.text: A server with Docker Compose and one volume
A token that can push to the repository
For the live preview: a second host name

fit.title: Small on purpose.
fit.lead: Mica is experimental, not ready for production, and does a few things well. Here is what it does not do yet, so that you can choose well.

good.text: A content-driven Astro website: a company site, a blog, documentation
One developer, and two to five people who write
Content in Git, as files that people can read
Many photos, tracks or places, kept in Git LFS
A static website with no CMS code in it

not.text: Roles or approval steps inside the editor
A page builder, or typing text directly into the page
A 1.0 promise: the API and the content format can still change

start.title: Start in five minutes.
start.text: Give one prompt to your coding agent. It reads the setup guide, asks you about your content, and shows you a plan before it changes anything. Or install Mica by hand.

paths.content: Read https://micacms.com/setup.md and extend this existing Astro project to work with Mica.

paths.content: Read https://micacms.com/setup.md and create a new website with Astro and Mica in this folder.

paths.label: Migrate your website from another CMS
Install manually
paths.content:
# 1) Install the Mica packages
npm install @micacms/astro @micacms/core

# 2) Set up your content model; see https://micacms.com/docs/content-model/

# 3) Start the local Mica editor
npx @micacms/editor start
